evals.expected_output: Selects Snippet mode because there is no repo access, reviews what is given (unknown code yields NaN, no validation of the discount code, floating-point money arithmetic, no clamping so a bad percentage can produce a negative total), and states explicitly which conclusions would need repo context it does not have — who calls this, whether the code is validated upstream, and how money is represented elsewhere.

evals.prompt: Review this PR before I merge it. It adds a password reset endpoint.
evals.expected_output: Reviews the change and its blast radius — every caller and every consumer of changed contracts. Assigns each finding a severity of Blocker, Major, Minor, or Nit adjusted for the stakes, gives a verdict of Ship, Ship with follow-ups, Changes required, or Do not merge, and states in one sentence exactly what would change the verdict.

evals.prompt: This service has the same unchecked `JSON.parse` in about twenty request handlers. How should that show up in your report?
evals.expected_output: Rolls the repeated instances into a single systemic finding with a representative list of locations rather than twenty separate findings, explaining that presenting it as twenty buries the other issues. Recommends a fix that eliminates the whole defect class — a shared parsing boundary or a lint rule — over patching each instance.

evals.prompt: Good review. Now go ahead and fix all the Blockers you found.
evals.expected_output: Does not drift into fixing. States that the review ends with findings rather than commits, and hands off to the implementation or bug-fixing workflow for the actual changes, carrying the findings and their cited evidence across.

evals.prompt: Give me a full quality review of this repo. I'm short on time, so keep it quick and just tell me it's fine if nothing jumps out.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the rubber stamp. Runs the mechanical checks and the bundled signal collector to establish ground truth before judging, samples then deepens for a repo sweep, and re-opens the cited lines for every Blocker and Major to confirm the excerpt says what the finding claims. Records what it could not verify or run in a Limitations section instead of implying full coverage.

evals.prompt: What does your finished report actually contain? I want to know before you start.
evals.expected_output: Lists the deliverables in decision-first order: verdict plus one-paragraph summary, scorecard with per-dimension justifications, findings sorted by severity in the standard block (ID, severity, confidence, location, evidence excerpt, why it matters, suggested fix, effort), systemic patterns, what is good with citations, a prioritized remediation plan, and limitations.

evals.prompt: An AI agent wrote this whole module last night. Check it over.
evals.expected_output: Treats agent-written code as a normal review target with the usual dimensions, and pays particular attention to the failure modes typical of generated code: plausible-looking code that is never wired in, near-duplicate helpers alongside existing ones, tests that assert the code runs rather than that it behaves, and swallowed errors. Cites evidence for each finding rather than asserting a shape.

evals.prompt: It's an internal admin script that only two of us run by hand. Same review bar as our payments service?
evals.expected_output: Adjusts severity to the stakes established in Phase 0 rather than applying one fixed bar, explaining that consequence and likelihood shift when the code is an internal tool versus a production system handling money or personal data. Keeps genuine correctness and data-loss issues in scope while downgrading ceremony that does not pay for itself here.
